title: Negotiation & Diplomacy
subtitle: Speak carefully, manage disagreement, and close a deal both sides can live with

lessons.title: Le langage diplomatique
lessons.description: Master the register of diplomacy: careful phrasing, understatement, and letting everyone save face.

blocks.heading: Le mot juste, jamais le mot cru
blocks.body: Diplomatic French does not lie; it selects. A skilled negotiator replaces a blunt judgment with a measured formula that leaves room for the other side to respond without losing standing. The goal is precision without cruelty: every word is weighed before it is spoken, and understatement (la litote) often carries more force than a direct attack.

examples.french: Votre offre est en deçà de nos attentes.
examples.english: Your offer falls short of our expectations.

examples.french: Ce chiffre nous laisse quelque peu perplexes.
examples.english: That figure leaves us somewhat puzzled.

examples.french: Nous entendons vos contraintes, sans pour autant les partager.
examples.english: We hear your constraints, without necessarily sharing them.

examples.french: Disons que la proposition mérite d'être retravaillée.
examples.english: Let's just say the proposal needs reworking.

blocks.tip: In negotiation French, the harsher the reality, the gentler the wrapping — decode "perplexe" as a polite word for "unacceptable".

blocks.heading: Sauver la face — protecting everyone's standing
blocks.body: A negotiation that humiliates the losing side rarely holds. Diplomatic speakers build an exit that lets the other party accept a concession without appearing weak: they credit a shared cause, cite external constraints, or leave a face-saving formula on the table. Amour-propre is never mocked, even when it is being managed.

examples.french: Ce n'est pas un recul de votre part, c'est une adaptation au contexte.
examples.english: This is not a step back on your part, it is an adaptation to the context.

examples.french: Personne ne perd la face si l'accord profite aux deux parties.
examples.english: No one loses face if the agreement benefits both sides.

examples.french: Elle a su ménager l'amour-propre de son interlocuteur tout en tenant sa position.
examples.english: She managed to spare her counterpart's pride while holding her position.

examples.french: Présentons cela comme une décision commune, pas comme une reculade.
examples.english: Let's present this as a joint decision, not as a climbdown.

blocks.tip: "Reculade" (climbdown) is a word you use about others, never about yourself — and never within earshot of the person who just conceded.

blocks.heading: L'implicite et le non-dit
blocks.body: Much of diplomatic meaning travels beneath the surface. A pause, a change of subject, or a sentence left unfinished can carry as much information as an explicit statement — and is far less costly to walk back. Reading the sous-entendu (the implication) accurately is as important as choosing your own words carefully.

examples.french: Son silence en disait plus long que n'importe quelle objection.
examples.english: Her silence said more than any objection could have.

examples.french: Il n'a rien affirmé explicitement, mais le sous-entendu était clair.
examples.english: He stated nothing explicitly, but the implication was clear.

examples.french: Restons volontairement dans l'ambiguïté sur ce point, pour l'instant.
examples.english: Let's deliberately stay ambiguous on that point, for now.

examples.french: Ce que l'on tait pèse parfois plus que ce que l'on dit.
examples.english: What is left unsaid sometimes carries more weight than what is said.

blocks.tip: A good negotiator can repeat a hostile sous-entendu back as a neutral question — it forces the other side to make their implication explicit, or drop it.

items.example: Restez diplomate, même si l'offre vous déçoit.
items.exampleEnglish: Stay diplomatic, even if the offer disappoints you.

items.example: Elle a trouvé une formule diplomatique pour refuser.
items.exampleEnglish: She found a diplomatic way to refuse.

items.example: La diplomatie consiste à dire non sans jamais prononcer ce mot.
items.exampleEnglish: Diplomacy consists of saying no without ever pronouncing that word.

items.english: the nuance, the shade of meaning
items.example: Toute la négociation tient dans cette nuance.
items.exampleEnglish: The whole negotiation hinges on that nuance.

items.english: to qualify, to add nuance to
items.example: Permettez-moi de nuancer ce que vient de dire mon collègue.
items.exampleEnglish: Allow me to qualify what my colleague just said.

items.example: Les échanges restaient feutrés malgré l'enjeu.
items.exampleEnglish: The exchanges stayed hushed despite what was at stake.

items.example: Elle a atténué son refus par une formule courtoise.
items.exampleEnglish: She softened her refusal with a courteous formula.

items.example: Son ton, toujours mesuré, désamorçait les tensions.
items.exampleEnglish: His tone, always measured, defused the tension.

items.example: Elle a annoncé le refus avec beaucoup de tact.
items.exampleEnglish: She announced the refusal with a great deal of tact.

items.english: to spare, to handle with care (feelings)
items.example: Un bon négociateur ménage l'amour-propre de son adversaire.
items.exampleEnglish: A good negotiator spares his opponent's pride.

items.example: L'accord lui a permis de sauver la face devant son conseil d'administration.
items.exampleEnglish: The agreement let him save face in front of his board.

items.example: Blesser l'amour-propre d'un partenaire compromet tout accord futur.
items.exampleEnglish: Wounding a partner's pride jeopardises any future agreement.

items.example: Elle a reformulé sa remarque pour ne pas froisser son homologue.
items.exampleEnglish: She rephrased her remark so as not to offend her counterpart.

items.example: Il n'avait pas l'intention de vous vexer, seulement de préciser un chiffre.
items.exampleEnglish: He had no intention of upsetting you, only of clarifying a figure.

items.example: Un bon médiateur connaît la susceptibilité de chaque partie.
items.exampleEnglish: A good mediator knows each side's touchiness.

items.example: Son homologue est réputé susceptible sur les questions de délai.
items.exampleEnglish: His counterpart is known to be touchy about deadline questions.

items.example: Face à la presse, la négociatrice pesait chacun de ses mots.
items.exampleEnglish: In front of the press, the negotiator weighed every one of her words.

items.example: Sa dernière phrase était pleine de sous-entendus.
items.exampleEnglish: His last sentence was full of insinuations.

items.example: Sans le dire, elle sous-entend que le prix est négociable.
items.exampleEnglish: Without saying so, she implies that the price is negotiable.

items.example: L'accord reste implicite tant que rien n'est signé.
items.exampleEnglish: The agreement remains implicit as long as nothing is signed.

items.example: Nous avons besoin d'un engagement explicite, pas d'un sous-entendu.
items.exampleEnglish: We need an explicit commitment, not an insinuation.

items.example: Toute la réunion reposait sur des non-dits.
items.exampleEnglish: The whole meeting rested on things left unsaid.

items.example: Sa réponse restait volontairement ambiguë.
items.exampleEnglish: Her answer remained deliberately ambiguous.

items.example: L'ambiguïté de la clause a été levée avant la signature.
items.exampleEnglish: The ambiguity of the clause was resolved before signing.

items.example: La prudence conseille de ne rien confirmer par écrit trop tôt.
items.exampleEnglish: Caution advises not confirming anything in writing too soon.

items.example: Il serait prudent de garder cette option ouverte.
items.exampleEnglish: It would be wise to keep that option open.

items.example: Il est resté circonspect tant que le contrat n'était pas signé.
items.exampleEnglish: He remained circumspect as long as the contract was not signed.

items.example: Le ton de l'échange est resté cordial du début à la fin.
items.exampleEnglish: The tone of the exchange stayed cordial from start to finish.

items.example: Les deux délégations sont restées courtoises malgré le désaccord.
items.exampleEnglish: Both delegations remained courteous despite the disagreement.

items.example: La courtoisie n'empêche pas la fermeté.
items.exampleEnglish: Courtesy does not preclude firmness.

items.example: Un malentendu sur les délais a failli tout compromettre.
items.exampleEnglish: A misunderstanding about the deadlines nearly compromised everything.

items.example: Un simple appel a suffi à dissiper le malentendu.
items.exampleEnglish: A simple phone call was enough to dispel the misunderstanding.

items.example: « Optimiste » était un euphémisme pour « irréaliste ».
items.exampleEnglish: "Optimistic" was a euphemism for "unrealistic".

items.example: « Ce n'est pas idéal » : une litote pour dire « c'est un échec ».
items.exampleEnglish: "It's not ideal": an understatement for "it's a failure".

items.example: Il faut formuler la demande sans donner l'impression d'exiger.
items.exampleEnglish: The request must be phrased without sounding like a demand.

items.english: an interlocutor, the person one is speaking with
items.example: Adaptez votre registre à votre interlocuteur.
items.exampleEnglish: Adapt your register to the person you are speaking with.

items.english: to sugarcoat, to water down (a message)
items.example: Il vaut mieux édulcorer l'annonce sans en trahir le fond.
items.exampleEnglish: It is better to sugarcoat the announcement without betraying its substance.

items.example: Sa retenue en dit parfois plus long qu'un long discours.
items.exampleEnglish: Her restraint sometimes says more than a long speech.

blocks.heading: Laisser entendre que, donner à penser que — insinuer sans affirmer
blocks.body: Diplomatic French has a family of verbs that convey a message without the speaker taking full responsibility for it: "laisser entendre que", "donner à penser que", "laisser supposer que". These take the indicative when the implication is presented as likely, but shift the following clause into cautious territory — the speaker can always retreat to "je n'ai jamais dit que...".

examples.french: Elle a laissé entendre que le budget pourrait augmenter.
examples.english: She let it be understood that the budget might increase.

examples.french: Son silence donnait à penser qu'il hésitait encore.
examples.english: His silence suggested he was still hesitating.

examples.french: Sans l'affirmer, il a laissé supposer que la clause serait retirée.
examples.english: Without stating it outright, he let it be assumed that the clause would be withdrawn.

examples.french: Je n'ai jamais dit que nous refuserions ; j'ai simplement laissé la question ouverte.
examples.english: I never said we would refuse; I simply left the question open.

blocks.tip: "Laisser entendre" is deniable by design — it is the grammatical equivalent of a raised eyebrow.

blocks.heading: Quoique et encore que — nuancer sans se contredire
blocks.body: "Quoique" (although, + subjunctive) opens a concession before it can be used against you; "encore que" (+ subjunctive, or indicative in careful speech) adds a qualifying afterthought once the main point has already landed. Both let a C1 speaker soften a position in real time, mid-sentence, without appearing to reverse it.

examples.french: Quoique l'offre soit intéressante, elle reste perfectible.
examples.english: Although the offer is interesting, it still has room for improvement.

examples.french: La proposition est raisonnable, encore qu'elle mérite d'être chiffrée plus précisément.
examples.english: The proposal is reasonable, though it deserves to be costed more precisely.

examples.french: Quoi qu'il en soit, restons ouverts à une nouvelle réunion.
examples.english: Be that as it may, let's remain open to another meeting.

examples.french: Il a raison, encore que je n'irais pas jusque-là.
examples.english: He is right, although I would not go that far.

blocks.tip: Do not confuse "quoique" (although, one word) with "quoi que" (whatever, two words) — both take the subjunctive, but they mean entirely different things.

items.prompt: Politely tell a supplier their offer is too low without insulting them.
items.french: Votre offre est en deçà de nos attentes, mais nous restons ouverts à la discussion.
items.english: Your offer falls short of our expectations, but we remain open to discussion.
items.tip: Keep "en deçà" light and fast: ahn duh-SAH — it should sound like a fact, not an accusation.

items.prompt: Frame a partner's concession as a shared decision, not a defeat.
items.french: Présentons cela comme une décision commune, pas comme une reculade.
items.english: Let's present this as a joint decision, not as a climbdown.
items.tip: Stress "commune" gently and let "reculade" fall — the contrast between the two words carries the whole idea.

items.prompt: Add a diplomatic qualification to an otherwise positive statement.
items.french: La proposition est raisonnable, encore qu'elle mérite d'être chiffrée plus précisément.
items.english: The proposal is reasonable, though it deserves to be costed more precisely.
items.tip: Pause slightly before "encore que" — the hesitation itself signals that a nuance is coming.

passages.title: Première rencontre entre Norderis et Solenza
passages.french:
Aurélie Vasseur, responsable des achats chez Norderis, reçut Karim Feddal dans une salle feutrée du siège lyonnais.
« Votre catalogue est riche, commença-t-elle, quoique certains tarifs nous laissent quelque peu perplexes. »
Karim, directeur commercial de Solenza, ne se froissa pas.
« J'entends votre remarque, répondit-il avec tact. Disons que nos prix reflètent une qualité que le marché ne compense pas toujours. »
« Je ne dis pas le contraire, nuança Aurélie. Mais votre offre reste, pour l'instant, en deçà de nos attentes en matière de délais. »
Un silence poli s'installa. Karim pesait ses mots avant de répondre.
« Ce que je peux vous laisser entendre, sans l'affirmer aujourd'hui, c'est qu'une marge de manœuvre existe sur les volumes. »
Aurélie sourit à demi : le sous-entendu était clair, sans qu'aucun chiffre eût été prononcé.
« Voilà une piste intéressante, dit-elle. Elle mériterait d'être creusée avant notre prochaine séance. »
« Avec plaisir, répondit Karim. Sachez toutefois que ma direction reste circonspecte sur tout ce qui touche aux pénalités de retard. »
« Rassurez-vous, dit Aurélie, notre intention n'est pas de vous piéger, mais de sécuriser les deux parties à parts égales. »
Karim hocha la tête, visiblement soulagé par cette précision.
« Voilà une nuance qui change tout, admit-il. Ce ne serait donc pas un recul de notre part, mais une adaptation au contexte. »
« Précisément, confirma-t-elle. Restons courtois, et voyons ce que nos équipes respectives peuvent chiffrer d'ici vendredi. »
Aucun accord n'avait été signé, mais aucune porte ne s'était fermée non plus — et c'était, dans ce genre de discussion feutrée, l'essentiel.
passages.english:
Aurélie Vasseur, head of purchasing at Norderis, received Karim Feddal in a hushed room at the Lyon headquarters.
"Your catalogue is rich," she began, "although some of your prices leave us somewhat puzzled."
Karim, sales director at Solenza, was not offended.
"I hear your remark," he replied tactfully. "Let's say our prices reflect a quality that the market does not always reward."
"I'm not saying otherwise," Aurélie qualified. "But your offer remains, for now, below our expectations regarding lead times."
A polite silence settled in. Karim weighed his words before answering.
"What I can let you understand, without stating it today, is that some room to manoeuvre exists on volumes."
Aurélie half-smiled: the implication was clear, without a single figure having been spoken.
"That's an interesting avenue," she said. "It would deserve to be explored before our next session."
"Gladly," Karim replied. "Do know, however, that my management remains circumspect about anything touching on late-delivery penalties."
"Rest assured," said Aurélie, "our intention is not to trap you, but to protect both parties equally."
Karim nodded, visibly relieved by that clarification.
"Now that's a nuance that changes everything," he admitted. "So this would not be a step back on our part, but an adaptation to the context."
"Precisely," she confirmed. "Let's stay courteous, and see what our respective teams can cost out by Friday."
No agreement had been signed, but no door had closed either — and in this kind of hushed discussion, that was the essential thing.

lessons.title: Gérer un désaccord difficile
lessons.description: Recognise a conflict before it hardens, and steer it toward resolution without losing your temper or the relationship.

blocks.heading: Reconnaître un désaccord qui s'envenime
blocks.body: Not every disagreement is dangerous, but some escalate quickly if left unaddressed. Watch for signs: the tone hardens, positions repeat instead of evolve, and each side starts defending its identity rather than its argument. A skilled negotiator names the shift early — before the discussion reaches an impasse.

examples.french: La discussion s'envenime depuis que le ton a changé.
examples.english: The discussion is turning sour since the tone changed.

examples.french: Nous sommes dans l'impasse : chacun campe sur ses positions.
examples.english: We are at a deadlock: each side is digging in.

examples.french: Cette réunion a viré à la confrontation personnelle.
examples.english: This meeting has turned into a personal confrontation.

examples.french: Un point de friction est apparu là où on ne l'attendait pas.
examples.english: A point of friction appeared where it was not expected.

blocks.tip: The moment someone says "c'est une question de principe" (it's a matter of principle), the disagreement has stopped being about facts — treat it accordingly.

blocks.heading: Désamorcer avant de convaincre
blocks.body: Trying to win an argument before lowering the temperature usually fails. Experienced negotiators desamorcer first — acknowledging the other person's frustration explicitly — before reintroducing substance. Active listening (l'écoute active) and reformulating the other side's point, even briefly, costs nothing and buys enormous goodwill.

examples.french: Je comprends que cette situation vous frustre ; reprenons calmement.
examples.english: I understand this situation frustrates you; let's start again calmly.

examples.french: Si je vous suis bien, votre inquiétude porte surtout sur le calendrier.
examples.english: If I follow you correctly, your concern is mainly about the timeline.

examples.french: Désamorçons ce point avant qu'il ne contamine le reste des discussions.
examples.english: Let's defuse this point before it contaminates the rest of the discussions.

examples.french: Prenons cinq minutes ; personne n'y perdra rien.
examples.english: Let's take five minutes; no one will lose anything by it.

blocks.tip: Reformulating an angry statement in neutral words ("donc, si je comprends bien...") forces both sides to hear the disagreement without its emotional charge.

blocks.heading: Rester ferme sans devenir intransigeant
blocks.body: Managing conflict well does not mean folding. A negotiator can hold a position with fermeté while remaining conciliant on form: separating the substance of a demand from the manner of stating it. The line between firmness and intransigeance is whether the other side still has room to respond.

examples.french: Je reste ferme sur ce point, mais je suis ouverte à en discuter la mise en œuvre.
examples.english: I remain firm on this point, but I am open to discussing how it is implemented.

examples.french: Son intransigeance a fini par braquer toute la salle contre lui.
examples.english: His intransigence eventually turned the whole room against him.

examples.french: Être conciliant sur la forme ne veut pas dire céder sur le fond.
examples.english: Being conciliatory on form does not mean giving in on substance.

examples.french: La fermeté, exprimée calmement, s'entend mieux que la colère.
examples.english: Firmness, expressed calmly, is heard better than anger.

blocks.tip: "Je comprends, mais" almost always sounds dismissive; "je comprends, et pourtant" keeps both truths in the room at once.

blocks.heading: Le subjonctif après le doute et le regret
blocks.body: When you voice disagreement, doubt or regret in careful French, the verb that follows almost always switches to the subjunctive: "je ne pense pas que", "il est regrettable que", "je doute que". This grammatical shift itself signals, before any content is even heard, that a reservation is coming — it prepares the listener.

examples.french: Je ne pense pas que cette solution soit tenable à long terme.
examples.english: I do not think this solution is sustainable in the long run.

examples.french: Il est regrettable que la discussion ait dérapé de cette façon.
examples.english: It is regrettable that the discussion went off the rails like that.

examples.french: Je doute que cette proposition satisfasse les deux parties.
examples.english: I doubt that this proposal will satisfy both sides.

examples.french: Il n'est pas certain que nous puissions trouver un terrain d'entente aujourd'hui.
examples.english: It is not certain that we can find common ground today.

blocks.tip: Switch "je pense que" (indicative) to "je ne pense pas que" (subjunctive) and your listener hears the change of mode before the change of meaning — a useful half-second of warning.

blocks.heading: En dépit de, quand bien même — tenir sa position avec élégance
blocks.body: "En dépit de" (+ noun, in spite of) and "quand bien même" (+ conditional, even if) let a C1 speaker acknowledge an obstacle while refusing to be derailed by it. "Quoi qu'il en soit" closes a difficult exchange without conceding the argument — it simply moves the conversation forward.

examples.french: En dépit du désaccord, nous devons avancer sur le reste de l'ordre du jour.
examples.english: In spite of the disagreement, we must move forward on the rest of the agenda.

examples.french: Quand bien même vous auriez raison sur ce détail, l'ensemble du dossier reste à revoir.
examples.english: Even if you were right about that detail, the whole file still needs revising.

examples.french: Quoi qu'il en soit, il faudra bien trancher avant vendredi.
examples.english: Be that as it may, a decision will have to be made before Friday.

examples.french: En dépit de sa fermeté apparente, il a fini par entendre nos arguments.
examples.english: In spite of his apparent firmness, he eventually heard our arguments.

blocks.tip: "Quand bien même" + conditional sounds almost literary — reserve it for moments when you want your firmness to sound composed, not aggressive.

passages.title: L'impasse sur les pénalités de retard
passages.french:
Trois semaines après leur première rencontre, Aurélie et Karim se retrouvèrent, mais l'atmosphère avait changé.
« Vos pénalités de retard sont excessives, lança Karim, la voix plus sèche qu'à l'accoutumée. C'est une question de principe. »
Aurélie sentit la discussion s'envenimer et choisit de ne pas répondre du tac au tac.
« Si je vous suis bien, reprit-elle, votre inquiétude porte surtout sur le montant, pas sur le principe lui-même. »
Karim marqua une pause ; la reformulation l'avait pris de court.
« C'est... en partie vrai, admit-il, un peu radouci. Mais nous campons sur nos positions depuis une heure. »
« Nous sommes dans l'impasse, en effet, concéda Aurélie. Prenons cinq minutes ; personne n'y perdra rien. »
À leur retour, Nadia Ghali, médiatrice engagée pour l'occasion, prit la parole avec calme.
« Ce point de friction n'a rien d'insurmontable, remarqua-t-elle, à condition d'écouter chacun jusqu'au bout. »
« Quoi qu'il en soit, ajouta-t-elle, il faudra bien trancher avant la fin de la journée. Karim, quel serait, selon vous, un seuil raisonnable ? »
Karim hésita, puis proposa un chiffre inférieur à sa demande initiale.
« Je reste ferme sur le principe des pénalités, répondit Aurélie, mais je suis ouverte à en discuter le montant exact. »
En dépit du désaccord persistant, un respect mutuel subsistait entre les deux négociateurs.
Nadia nota les deux positions sans trancher elle-même, et proposa de reprendre la discussion le lendemain, à tête reposée.
En quittant la salle, Karim reconnut, presque malgré lui, que l'intransigeance n'avait jamais fait avancer un dossier.
passages.english:
Three weeks after their first meeting, Aurélie and Karim met again, but the atmosphere had changed.
"Your late-delivery penalties are excessive," Karim said, his voice drier than usual. "It's a matter of principle."
Aurélie felt the discussion turning sour and chose not to snap back immediately.
"If I follow you correctly," she resumed, "your concern is mainly about the amount, not the principle itself."
Karim paused; the reformulation had caught him off guard.
"That's... partly true," he admitted, somewhat softened. "But we've been digging in for an hour."
"We are at a deadlock indeed," Aurélie conceded. "Let's take five minutes; no one will lose anything by it."
When they returned, Nadia Ghali, a mediator hired for the occasion, spoke up calmly.
"This point of friction is not insurmountable," she remarked, "provided everyone is heard out fully."
"Be that as it may," she added, "a decision will have to be made before the end of the day. Karim, what would you consider a reasonable threshold?"
Karim hesitated, then proposed a figure lower than his initial demand.
"I remain firm on the principle of penalties," Aurélie replied, "but I am open to discussing the exact amount."
In spite of the persisting disagreement, mutual respect remained between the two negotiators.
Nadia noted both positions without deciding herself, and suggested resuming the discussion the next day, with a clearer head.
Leaving the room, Karim admitted, almost despite himself, that intransigence had never moved a file forward.

lessons.title: Trouver un compromis
lessons.description: Move from position to proposal, trade concessions wisely, and close a deal both sides will actually honour.

blocks.heading: De la position à la proposition
blocks.body: A position states what you want; a proposal states a way to get there that the other side can accept. Skilled negotiators translate rigid positions into flexible proposals early, because a proposal can be countered, adjusted and improved — a position can only be accepted or rejected.

examples.french: Plutôt qu'une position, voici une proposition concrète à étudier.
examples.english: Rather than a position, here is a concrete proposal to consider.

examples.french: Et si nous envisagions une contre-proposition sur les volumes ?
examples.english: What if we considered a counter-proposal on the volumes?

examples.french: Cette proposition tient compte de vos contraintes, tout en préservant les nôtres.
examples.english: This proposal takes your constraints into account, while preserving ours.

examples.french: Aboutir à un accord suppose que chacun bouge un peu.
examples.english: Reaching an agreement requires that everyone move a little.

blocks.tip: "Et si..." (what if...) is the softest way to float a proposal in French — it invites collaboration instead of demanding a decision.

blocks.heading: Céder du terrain sans tout céder
blocks.body: A concession is not a defeat if it is traded, not simply given. Naming the exchange explicitly — "nous cédons ceci, en contrepartie de cela" — turns a one-sided sacrifice into a visible, mutual transaction. The goal is a compromis that both parties can defend afterward to their own side.

examples.french: Nous pouvons céder du terrain sur le prix, en contrepartie d'un engagement sur la durée.
examples.english: We can give ground on price, in exchange for a commitment on duration.

examples.french: Cette concession n'a de sens que si elle est réciproque.
examples.english: This concession only makes sense if it is reciprocal.

examples.french: Un compromis mutuellement avantageux vaut mieux qu'une victoire à sens unique.
examples.english: A mutually beneficial compromise is worth more than a one-sided victory.

examples.french: Renoncer à ce point nous permet d'obtenir satisfaction sur l'essentiel.
examples.english: Giving up that point allows us to get satisfaction on what matters most.

blocks.tip: Never announce a concession without immediately naming what you expect in return — silence there reads as weakness, not generosity.

blocks.heading: Sceller l'accord
blocks.body: Once terms are agreed, C1 French shifts to the vocabulary of closing: finaliser, entériner, ratifier, signer. This final stage still requires care — an accord acted on in good faith holds better than one merely imposed, so the closing conversation confirms mutual understanding before any signature.

examples.french: Récapitulons les termes avant de finaliser l'accord.
examples.english: Let's recap the terms before finalising the agreement.

examples.french: Ce compromis satisfait les deux parties ; il ne reste qu'à le signer.
examples.english: This compromise satisfies both parties; all that remains is to sign it.

examples.french: Le conseil devra entériner cet accord la semaine prochaine.
examples.english: The board will have to endorse this agreement next week.

examples.french: Une fois l'accord scellé, chacun devra en respecter la lettre autant que l'esprit.
examples.english: Once the deal is sealed, everyone will need to respect both its letter and its spirit.

blocks.tip: "Il ne reste qu'à le signer" is the classic closing line of a French negotiation — say it only when you mean it, since backtracking after it lands badly.

blocks.heading: À condition que, pourvu que — poser ses conditions
blocks.body: Proposing a compromise means stating conditions precisely. "À condition que" and "pourvu que" (+ subjunctive) attach a concession to a requirement in a single elegant clause, softer than a blunt "si" clause because it presents the requirement as a shared threshold to clear together, not an ultimatum.

examples.french: Nous acceptons cette clause, à condition que les délais soient garantis par écrit.
examples.english: We accept this clause, provided the deadlines are guaranteed in writing.

examples.french: Le compromis tient, pourvu que chacun respecte sa part de l'accord.
examples.english: The compromise holds, provided everyone honours their part of the agreement.

examples.french: Nous pouvons revoir le prix, à condition que le volume augmente en conséquence.
examples.english: We can revisit the price, provided the volume increases accordingly.

examples.french: Pourvu que les deux parties y trouvent leur compte, la forme importe peu.
examples.english: Provided both parties find it worthwhile, the form matters little.

blocks.tip: "À condition que" reads as collaborative; "si" alone can sound like a threat in a tense negotiation — reach for the subjunctive clause when the stakes are high.

blocks.heading: Le conditionnel passé pour évoquer ce qui aurait pu se passer
blocks.body: Once a deal is close, negotiators often use the past conditional to acknowledge a road not taken, without reopening it: "nous aurions pu exiger davantage, mais...". This closes a topic gracefully while quietly reminding the other side of the concession already made — useful leverage delivered without confrontation.

examples.french: Nous aurions pu exiger davantage, mais nous privilégions une relation durable.
examples.english: We could have demanded more, but we prefer a lasting relationship.

examples.french: Sans cette concession, l'accord n'aurait jamais vu le jour.
examples.english: Without that concession, the agreement would never have come about.

examples.french: Vous auriez pu refuser ; vous avez choisi de négocier, et nous vous en savons gré.
examples.english: You could have refused; you chose to negotiate, and we are grateful for that.

examples.french: Un compromis plus rapide aurait sans doute coûté plus cher aux deux parties.
examples.english: A faster compromise would probably have cost both parties more.

blocks.tip: The past conditional lets you remind a partner of your own generosity exactly once, elegantly — repeating it turns gratitude-seeking into resentment.

passages.title: La signature, enfin
passages.french:
Un mois après l'impasse sur les pénalités, Aurélie et Karim se retrouvèrent une dernière fois, accompagnés de Nadia Ghali.
« Voici notre proposition finale, annonça Aurélie. Nous renonçons à la pénalité automatique, à condition que Solenza garantisse un délai maximal par écrit. »
Karim consulta brièvement ses notes avant de répondre.
« Et si nous ajoutions une contrepartie ? Nous acceptons ce délai maximal, en échange d'un engagement de volume sur deux ans. »
« Voilà une contre-proposition raisonnable, reconnut Aurélie. Un compromis mutuellement avantageux, plutôt qu'une victoire à sens unique. »
Nadia sourit : le terrain d'entente qu'elle avait patiemment cherché à faire émerger semblait enfin trouvé.
« Nous aurions pu exiger davantage sur le prix, admit Karim, mais nous privilégions une relation durable avec Norderis. »
« Pourvu que chacun respecte sa part de l'accord, répondit Aurélie, la forme importe peu. Récapitulons les termes avant de finaliser. »
Ensemble, ils relurent chaque clause, ajustant ici un mot, précisant là une date.
Aucune clause ne restait ambiguë ; chacun savait exactement ce qu'il devait à l'autre.
« Ce compromis satisfait les deux parties, conclut Nadia. Il ne reste qu'à le signer. »
Karim et Aurélie échangèrent une poignée de main ferme avant de signer, chacun de son côté, l'accord final.
Le conseil d'administration de Norderis devrait encore entériner l'accord, mais personne, dans la salle, n'en doutait plus.
En sortant, Nadia nota que le meilleur compromis n'est jamais celui qui satisfait tout le monde à moitié, mais celui que chacun défend ensuite comme le sien.
passages.english:
A month after the deadlock over the penalties, Aurélie and Karim met one last time, accompanied by Nadia Ghali.
"Here is our final proposal," Aurélie announced. "We are waiving the automatic penalty, provided Solenza guarantees a maximum lead time in writing."
Karim briefly checked his notes before answering.
"What if we added a trade-off? We accept that maximum lead time, in exchange for a two-year volume commitment."
"Now that's a reasonable counter-proposal," Aurélie acknowledged. "A mutually beneficial compromise, rather than a one-sided victory."
Nadia smiled: the common ground she had patiently tried to help emerge finally seemed to have been found.

"Provided everyone honours their part of the agreement," Aurélie replied, "the form matters little. Let's recap the terms before finalising."
Together, they reread every clause, adjusting a word here, specifying a date there.
No clause remained ambiguous; each side knew exactly what it owed the other.
"This compromise satisfies both parties," Nadia concluded. "All that remains is to sign it."
Karim and Aurélie exchanged a firm handshake before signing, each on their own side, the final agreement.
Norderis's board would still have to endorse the agreement, but no one in the room doubted it any longer.
